To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a fast multi-resolution tree-based algorithm that can be used to detect landmarks in 2D images.
we propose variants of a tree-based approach for fast and accurate landmark detection in 2d bioimages.

1) our method variants are generic, fast, and robust; 2) they are competitive with existing methods; 3) we provide parameter configuration rules and datasets to foster their use; 4) we integrate the algorithms in the open-source software Cytomine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of landmarks on bioimages, which is a necessary but time-consuming step in geometric morphometrics.
the development of a new method for landmark detection, its evaluation, and its integration into a software framework.
the automatic recognition of anatomical landmarks from 2D images.

the proposed approach is a good alternative to existing methods and that its performance can be improved by fine tuning the method parameters.
the proposed approach is a generic and fast method for the detection of anatomical landmark in bioimages.
the method proposed here is fast, generic and achieves competitive results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our method achieves state-of-the-art performances for the detection of anatomical structures in bioimages and that our method is generic, fast, and easy to use.
our method is generic, fast, and competitive with respect to current existing methods.
our method achieves competitive performances with respect to existing methods while being fast and generic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tree-based approach can be successfully applied to the landmark detection task in bioimages and is competitive with existing approaches.
the proposed approach is fast and robust, and can be easily used by end-users to detect anatomical landmarks in a wide variety of images.
the multi-resolution tree-based method is an efficient and generic approach for the landmark recognition in 2D images.
